system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Cabela's Incorporated realized record after acquisition by Bass Pro Group, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the acquired company deregistered its
> securities shortly after closing and its acquirer is privately held with no separate
> SEC disclosure of the acquired business, there is no post-closing public 10-K for this
> entity; the realized record traced here is limited to the deregistration filing itself
> and reputable press covering the roughly two-to-five-year period following the
> September 2017 closing. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the
> transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On October 10, 2017, Cabela's Incorporated filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination
  of registration of its Class A Common Stock under Section 12(g) of the Securities
  Exchange Act, stating an approximate number of holders of record of 1 as of the
  certification date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-306982, Form 15-12B]
- EDGAR's filing history for Cabela's Incorporated (CIK 0001267130) shows no Form 10-K
  or other periodic annual report filed after the Form 10-K for fiscal year 2016 (filed
  2017-02-16); no subsequent annual report has been filed. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001267130&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40]
- A search of SEC EDGAR company records for "Bass Pro" returns no periodic-report filer
  (no 10-K, 10-Q, or 20-F filer) under that name; the acquirer that took Cabela's private
  does not appear to separately register with or report to the SEC. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=bass+pro&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=100]
- Consequently, there is no public, audited 3-5-year financial or segment record for the
  acquired business, and the facts below are limited to what reputable press has
  reported about operational changes following the transaction; the realized financial
  outcome for this case is **not publicly observable** and is coded accordingly.

## Documented post-closing operational changes (press-sourced)
- In a statement reported in early March 2019, the acquirer announced it would close a
  distribution center in Sidney, Nebraska (the former headquarters community) and a
  merchandise return center in Oshkosh, Nebraska, affecting a combined 162 positions
  (121 at the Sidney facility, 41 at Oshkosh), as part of "an extensive review of all
  Bass Pro Shops and Cabela's operations." [SRC: https://sgbonline.com/bass-pro-shuttering-facilities-in-sidney-oshkosh-in-nebraska/]
- That same report stated the Sidney distribution facility, originally built during
  World War II, had been in operation 77 years and was found to handle the least volume
  of the combined company's distribution centers, and that the company said it "remains
  committed to maintaining a presence in Sidney." [SRC: https://sgbonline.com/bass-pro-shuttering-facilities-in-sidney-oshkosh-in-nebraska/]
- On January 13, 2020, the company announced the closure of the Cabela's retail
  locations in Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia and Bristol, Virginia, consolidating each into a
  nearby Bass Pro Shops location, stating "we can better serve our customers with
  greater product assortment, value and local expertise in a single location." [SRC: https://sgbonline.com/cabelas-closing-north-georgia-store/]
- A local news report on the same Fort Oglethorpe/East Ridge consolidation quoted the
  company's statement that "Two large format stores located just 2.4 miles apart are not
  necessary to serve our customers in the Greater Chattanooga area," and reported that
  "virtually all Cabela's team members are being offered the opportunity to transfer to
  the new location." [SRC: https://wdef.com/2020/01/13/catoosa-cabelas-closing-merge-bass-pro-shops-location]
- A Site Selection Magazine feature (undated in the retrieved copy, but referencing
  events in the months following the September 2017 closing) reported that the
  acquirer intended to keep "up to 125 IT jobs and some accounting personnel" at the
  former Cabela's Sidney campus, that roughly 800 employees remained at that campus at
  the time of reporting (down from an employment peak of about 2,000), and that "most of
  the remaining positions would either transfer to Missouri or be phased out during the
  consolidation." [SRC: https://siteselection.com/sidneys-next-saga-finding-jobs-to-replace-those-lost-to-cabelas-bass-pro-merger/]
- The same feature reported that the acquirer's CEO pledged to donate up to $10 million
  of his own money to a severance fund for laid-off Sidney employees, and asked former
  Cabela's executives who received "golden parachutes" in the sale to contribute to that
  fund. [SRC: https://siteselection.com/sidneys-next-saga-finding-jobs-to-replace-those-lost-to-cabelas-bass-pro-merger/]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- General industry commentary describes the acquirer as a privately held retailer that
  does not publicly disclose consolidated or segment-level sales and profitability
  figures; any post-closing revenue or profitability figures attributed to the combined
  enterprise in secondary sources are not traceable to an audited primary filing and are
  recorded here as [UNVERIFIED]. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because Cabela's Incorporated deregistered its securities on October 10, 2017 and its
  acquirer is privately held with no identified SEC periodic-report filing, there is no
  public 3-5-year audited outcome record for this business; the outcome is coded
  **uncertain** on that basis. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-306982, Form 15-12B]
- The traceable press record for the roughly two-to-five-year period following the
  September 2017 closing documents facility and headcount contraction at the former
  target's home base (a 77-year-old Sidney, NE distribution center and the Oshkosh, NE
  return center closed in 2019, affecting 162 jobs; corporate-campus headcount reported
  down from about 2,000 at peak to about 800, with most remaining roles slated to
  transfer to the acquirer's Missouri headquarters or be phased out) and store-network
  consolidation (Fort Oglethorpe, GA and Bristol, VA Cabela's locations closed and
  merged into nearby Bass Pro Shops locations in January 2020), alongside stated
  intentions by the acquirer to retain a reduced footprint in Sidney and to fund a
  severance program for displaced employees. [SRC: https://sgbonline.com/bass-pro-shuttering-facilities-in-sidney-oshkosh-in-nebraska/] [SRC: https://sgbonline.com/cabelas-closing-north-georgia-store/] [SRC: https://siteselection.com/sidneys-next-saga-finding-jobs-to-replace-those-lost-to-cabelas-bass-pro-merger/]

[SLICE END]
